instructions: Update the relevant source document and this plan together when a decision, order or measured result changes.

versions.name: V1-PROOF
versions.summary: The current HUX: a small two-wheel robot with its legs locked at 30°, to prove balance, manual drive and fault handling for strictly less than $1,000. Powered hips return in the next version.

focus.title: Finish the R05 body and the second wheel channel
focus.summary: R05 is the current build. The user reports an assembled frame and hip holes that agree with the guide. V1-PROOF has no powered hips: both legs stay locked at 30°, and the two wheel gearmotors are the only powered axes. Plate 4 is in print, and plate 5 is next. Order the second gearmotor, the second driver, the wheels and a battery if necessary.

nextActions.title: Finish the R05 assembly with locked legs
nextActions.detail: The hip holes agree with the guide, per the user. When plate 4 is complete, install the struts and the carriers, and lock both legs at 30°. Install the gearmotors and the wheels when they arrive. The servo cradles are optional. Record each value in the R05 fit record.

nextActions.detail: Order one Pololu 4752 gearmotor ($60.95), one Pololu 4035 driver ($11.94), two Pololu 3278 wheels ($8.86 each) and two Pololu 2674 adapters ($7.75 each). Prices are goods only, checked on 2026-10-16. Buy a 3S pack of approximately 2.2 Ah, maximum 106 × 35 × 25 mm, only if no compatible pack and charger are on hand. nextActions.title: Run the electronics bench, stages E0–E6
nextActions.detail: The user is ready for bench tests. Flash the prebuilt hux_bench.uf2, start the host console and follow the electronics bench guide: toolchain and blink, IMU identity and raw data, encoder counts, driver and motor jog, wheel speed loop, fault checks and the tilt-follow routine. Record each stage in a dated session record, because no stage is closed.

nextActions.title: Build and test the kill chain
nextActions.detail: Order the Pololu 2813 rail switch, a 74HC14, a 3.3 V regulator, the diodes, the passives and two momentary buttons. Build the circuit on a small board. Run stages K0–K6 with the wheel lifted after stage E5. The design is a proposal, and no part is ordered.

nextActions.title: Identify the received parts and outstanding arrivals
nextActions.detail: Record the gearmotor/driver labels, the total received driver count, the dimensions and the condition. The receipt covers one Pololu 4752 gearmotor and one DRV8874 driver (Pololu 4035), but R05 needs two of each. The Pico 2 and the LSM6DSO IMU are received. The two ST3215 servos are received and stay in stock for the next version.

nextActions.title: Confirm controls and power interfaces
nextActions.detail: The Pico 2 and the DRV8874 drivers are received, but the total driver count remains to record. The LSM6DSO IMU is received, untested. Confirm the encoder level conversion, the harness and the protected power rails. Record the bench-supply ratings. V1-PROOF needs no servo interface.

nextActions.title: Resolve power and return-energy protection
nextActions.detail: Prepare a fused harness and an independent actuator-power cut. Verify the supply behavior, the current limits and a regeneration path before you lower a load, backdrive an actuator or reverse aggressively.

criteria: Record exact parts, variants, quantities, costs and reusable stock.
Quote missing items and retain reserves inside the strict cash cap.
Check mass allocations and the full wheel, motor, bearing, battery and cable envelopes.
Detail the pinned structure with both legs locked at 30°.

milestones.title: Supported wheels and pinned chassis
milestones.summary: Qualify the wheel channels and the basic electronics before the first free-standing balance attempt.
criteria: Build supported axles, pinned neutral legs, rest skids and a catch fixture.
Verify motor/encoder polarity, current limits, low-voltage response and thermal behavior.
Do tests of the physical kill, watchdog, reset, stale commands and sensor faults with deliberate rearm.
Measure assembled mass, center of mass, timing and power behavior.

milestones.title: Pinned-leg balance and manual drive
milestones.summary: Prove two-wheel mobility with both legs mechanically pinned at neutral.
criteria: Hold balance for 60 seconds in at least 9 of 10 starts without support contact.
Complete logged 2 m forward/reverse runs, left/right arcs and both 360° in-place turns under the physical protocol.
Complete five combined sequences at bounded speed, on the required floors and voltages.
Keep the failures and the configuration hashes. Simulated success does not close this gate.

milestones.title: Complete the physical proof
milestones.summary: Close the measured mobility, disturbance, fault, duty, mass and budget gates before you expand the scope.
criteria: Qualify the specified 0.8 N·s longitudinal and 0.4 N·s lateral pulses, both signs and durations.
Qualify separate 3° slopes, 5 mm smooth bumps and 3 mm seam fixtures at 0.15 m/s.
Complete a 10-minute mixed balance and drive session in the measured electrical and thermal limits, with no resets.
Record final mass ≤3.0 kg and all-in new cash < $1,000.
Archive the logs, videos and failure counts. Replace the model assumptions with measurements and rerun the matrix.

bench.title: Electronics and wheel bench
bench.summary: The bench for V1-PROOF is the Pico 2, the IMU and one wheel channel. The single-leg bench is parked for the next version. Follow the electronics bench guide, then the kill chain stages.

stages.title: Toolchain and blink
stages.action: Flash the bench firmware and open the host console.
stages.evidence: A Hux C/C++ build runs on the Pico 2 and prints over USB serial.

stages.title: IMU identity and raw data
stages.action: Connect the IMU with seven wires and read the identity register.
stages.evidence: WHO_AM_I reads 0x6C. A stationary log and a six-face check are recorded.

stages.title: Encoder counts
stages.action: Power the encoder at 5 V through the level conversion. Turn the output shaft one revolution by hand.
stages.evidence: One turn gives 1920 ±4 counts with the correct sign.

stages.title: Driver and motor jog
stages.action: Connect the DRV8874 driver. Do the static checks. Jog the lifted wheel at low duty.
stages.evidence: The lifted wheel turns in both directions, and the encoder sign agrees.

stages.title: Fault checks
stages.action: Test a stale command, USB loss, a reset and the physical cut.

stages.title: Tilt-follow routine
stages.action: Tilt the IMU by hand with the wheel lifted.
stages.evidence: The wheel follows the IMU pitch in the correct direction, with the log.

New sheets EL-06 and EL-07 give a cut length for each of nineteen bundles and the loading of every connector. JST XH 2.50 mm is the connector standard, with XT30 for the 12 V path. focus.title: Let measured proof results define the next version
focus.summary: Powered hips and leg-height change return in this version. Carry forward the measured actuator and sensor behavior, the telemetry, the fault handling and the test evidence. Future full-size Hux has a stated RobStride direction, but no RobStride order or third-version hardware release is established.

nextActions.title: Close and archive the V1-PROOF evidence
nextActions.detail: Complete the physical acceptance gates and preserve logs, videos, failure counts and firmware/model revisions before you select expanded requirements.

nextActions.title: Make an explicit next-version scope decision
nextActions.detail: Choose the third version’s name, requirements, architecture and budget from the proof’s measured results. V1 success does not promise a stair upgrade of the proof chassis.

nextActions.title: Design the powered hips
nextActions.detail: Each inner ST3215 servo turns a crank on its output disc. A 40 mm RC pushrod moves the upper link, ratio 2.6 to 3.1 : 1. The R05 kit has the servo frame, the crank hub, the wall bushing, the upper link with a boss and two drill jigs (plate 6). V1-PROOF keeps the legs locked.

milestones.title: Powered leg-height adjustment
milestones.summary: Moved from V1-PROOF on 2026-10-16. Add the supported 3:1 reductions after the pinned-leg balance. Qualify each leg before synchronized movement.
criteria: Qualify the 0.75 N·m mounted servo hold for 10 minutes. Qualify the separate 1.0 N·m short transient target.
Measure backlash, loaded clearance and pose-dependent pitch trim.
Complete ten low/high/low cycles with both wheels loaded. The target is at least 25 mm of actual body-height change.
Make sure that there is no support contact, overload or balance loss. Use the measured qualified range.

bench.title: Single-leg bench exercise
bench.summary: Parked on 2026-10-16. The user removed the powered hips from V1-PROOF and dropped the one-leg requirement. This bench returns with the powered legs of the next version.

geometry.label: Links
geometry.value: 2 × 110 mm struts from rear hips, slanted forward

geometry.label: Wheel
geometry.value: 100 mm nominal; lifted for first powered tests

stages.title: Identify received parts
stages.action: Identify the received gearmotor/driver labels, the total driver count, the printed revision/material, the dimensions and the condition. The receipt and the print alone do not complete this stage.
stages.evidence: A confirmed inventory and a marked wiring diagram. The template is updated for the actual parts.

stages.title: Power and readback
stages.action: Check the disconnected rails and the polarity. Secure the bare servo. Verify the disabled startup and read the feedback. Read the encoder counts with the motor power off.
stages.evidence: Stable communications, expected counts per measured wheel revolution, and a verified independent power cut.

stages.title: Bare servo
stages.action: Verify the startup and the target mapping first. Then command ±5° at the servo output at maximum 5°/s with the hub, the pushrod and the load removed.
stages.evidence: Correct direction with no startup jump, reset, unexpected current or tracking fault.

stages.title: Passive linkage
stages.action: Preserve the user report of satisfactory travel. Add measured endpoints, closest clearances and neutral free play. Recheck the lateral stack after the R03 carrier and lock link replace the R01 parts.
stages.evidence: The recorded distance between centers, the retained fastener stack, and photos that show no binding or hardware contact through the hand sweep. The powered-fixture catch and the load capacity remain separate checks.

stages.title: Small driven leg cycles
stages.action: Align at 30° with the power off. Remove the lock before you arm the system. Start 28–32° at 1°/s and hold 2 seconds at each end.
stages.evidence: Ten small cycles with independently measured angle, no jump or binding, and logged current, voltage and temperature.

stages.title: Wider unloaded travel
stages.action: After small-cycle success, try 25–35° and expand only in the measured clearance and stop margins.
stages.evidence: Repeatable endpoints, measured vertical/fore-aft travel and approach-direction backlash. No stop strikes.

stages.title: Wheel alone
stages.action: Pin the leg, keep the wheel lifted and keep the servo torque off. Verify the sign. Then try +10 rpm → 0 → −10 rpm, and wait for measured zero before the reversal.
stages.evidence: Stable low-speed response with the correct feedback sign. No reset or overvoltage. Record the stiction before you raise the limits.

stages.title: Fault behavior
stages.action: In the supported small-motion envelope, do tests of the deadman release, lost commands/feedback, reset, lost servo communication and physical kill.
stages.evidence: Faults latch, the catch contains torque loss, the cut works without software, and reconnection never rearms automatically.

stages.title: Combined unloaded motion
stages.action: After separate and fault tests, slowly sweep 28–32° while the lifted wheel turns at 10 rpm.
stages.evidence: Five repeatable cycles with no dropped commands, resets, wire snags or rail violations.

stages.title: Measured loading
stages.action: Add a captured, measured load only after the electrical and thermal gates. Add the load in steps with a known force direction and lever arm.
stages.evidence: Record the deflection, backlash, temperature and rail behavior under load, with a supported power loss. The later torque/duty qualification remains separate.
